backgrounds: A single set for the entire episode: a warm, upper-middle-class open-plan home living room shot from a fixed camera angle. The two stop-motion characters sit side by side on a light grey/taupe fabric sofa. Behind them is a softly blurred open-plan interior: a beige hallway wall with a white door, a floor lamp with a fabric shade glowing warmly on the left, a framed photo on a shelf in the far background-left, and to the right a staircase with white railing leading up, a kitchen with white cabinetry and under-cabinet lighting, and a dining table with dark chairs. A dark flat-screen TV edge is visible at the far left foreground. The black title-card background (used for the intro/outro logo bumper) is the only other 'location,' functioning as a graphic slate rather than a physical set.
props: Smartphone (held by the female character, screen-lit, central to the story/plot device)
TV remote control (held by the male character)
Grey fabric sofa/armchair with visible stitching and a rolled/tufted armrest
Floor lamp with warm glowing fabric shade
Framed photograph on a background shelf

lighting_notes: Warm, cozy interior lighting consistent throughout: practical sources (floor lamp, under-cabinet kitchen lights) motivate soft golden highlights on the felt character models, while the room falls into a naturalistic soft-focus falloff toward the background. Lighting stays static scene-to-scene since it is a single continuous shot/set, reinforcing a homey, intimate, sitcom-living-room mood. The title/outro cards are pure black with no lighting, used as a stark graphic contrast to the warm live scene.
color_palette: warm skin-tone peach/salmon (male character felt skin)
charcoal black (male character's coat/suit, female's pants)
golden yellow (title card text and ribbon graphic, on black)
visual_complexity_notes: The living scene is moderately detailed but deliberately shallow-focus: the couch and characters are in sharp focus while the layered background (hallway, staircase, kitchen, dining area) is softly blurred, so the environment reads as a believable, lived-in home without competing for attention. This is a deliberate depth-of-field choice that keeps all visual and comedic focus on the two characters' faces and the phone screen, which is where the joke/story plays out. The bookend title cards are the opposite extreme: flat, minimal, single-color black backgrounds with bold yellow/white typography, creating a clean graphic 'stage curtain' effect around the single-set live-action-style stop-motion scene.
